utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The trial is ready to proceed. The Bench has noticed that Mr. Simic is not in the courtroom. I would like to find out whether there is any information from Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Actually, we are as surprised as the Trial Chamber is, because we have had no information whatsoever prior to this moment that our client will not appear in the court. We had a meeting with our client, I believe on Thursday, Friday -- Friday, in the afternoon, and it was -- we were told by our client that he will appear in the court. And as far as I know, he is willing to -- he is not waiving his right to be present in the courtroom -- of presence in the courtroom during the testimony of the next witness, [redacted], and as well as this witness, concerning the A and B document. I can probably check it out, but I was already in the courtroom when I found out -- when I found out that my client is not coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber is informed that the Registry has made arrangements for the videolink, one-way videolink, whereby Mr. Milan Simic can remain in the detention unit and follow the proceedings from here, but we cannot watch him, and that he will be given a telephone link to yourself, Mr. Zecevic, for continuation -- for any communication he may wish to make, but there was no instruction from the Trial Chamber that the fact that that is ongoing, then he should not be brought to court. So we are also taken by surprise. So maybe we will adjourn, allow to you make contact and find out what the position is. We are aware, from the information from the Legal Officer, that the Prosecution is beginning with the witness on Variant A and B, the documents that have been pending for sometime, and maybe you can have instructions from him just for that purpose, and then we will see what transpired later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will do that immediately as we are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we will rise to allow to you do that, and then you can inform the Court attendants as to what the position is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Court will rise. --- Break taken at 2.29 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I talked with my client just a couple of minutes ago, and he waived his right to be present during the testimony of the witness B. O'Donnell concerning the A and B documents but he actually did not waive his present -- to be present during the start-up of the testimony of the next witness, [redacted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. I think let's go ahead with the Variant A and B issue, and then we'll discussion what arrangements can be made later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours, please, my colleague Ms. Reidy will handle the issue of the Variant A and B document and produce the evidence relating to that. But perhaps before that takes place, there's just one or two matters that I think I ought to raise at this juncture. And I'll be very brief. Firstly, on the issue of translations, I can tell the Chamber that the Prosecution documents that were untranslated have now been translated. And I will at an appropriate moment produce them. They are in fact P37, P38, P39, and P41. But rather than produce them now, I'll do that at a later stage to ensure that this afternoon goes a bit smoothly. Secondly, the Prosecution has collated all the Defence material, all the Defence documents produced to us by all Defence counsel. We have produced a set of box files or binders which contain all of the Defence material. It's now undergone the process whereby it's been given an ERN number. That's a computer number that identifies a particular document. And we've made four copies of these sets of binders. We propose to deliver those to the Defence. The only issue that arises is that of course it will contain defence material from one Defence team and defence material from another Defence team and so on, and so therefore one Defence team's materials may be revealed to another Defence team, because it's all contained in the one set of documents. So I'll call upon the Defence to let us know sooner rather than later if they have any objection to that. I hope not, because the effect of that is to collect all of the Defence material. We'll all be able to go straight to the document once the Defence produce it, and it will make life just so much easier in dealing with these documents. So that's the second issue that I wanted to raise. And I hope that they'll be able to give us an indication hopefully in the next 24/48 hours what their view is about us handing over to them these four sets of collated Defence documents. And finally, one last matter, the issue of Esad Dagovic. You'll recall that he was the witness who remains to be cross-examined by the Defence. We have contacted him. Because of his personal commitments, he can only give evidence on Wednesday. He's now come some four times, I think, to the Tribunal and is experiencing difficulties with his employment, even though he lives in a nearby country. And because of that, I'm going to ask for the Chamber's indulgence in allowing the Prosecution to call him on Wednesday and if necessary interpose him in the evidence of another witness. So that's a matter, I think, that the Chamber should let us know fairly soon so that if you are not minded to grant the application, then we can make alternative arrangements. But that is our application, that we would like to call him and get his cross-examination over and done with on Wednesday if possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think on the last point on the witness who is coming, he's a protected witness. He's got a pseudonym, isn't he? So -- isn't he the one who is a protected witness? MR. DI FAZIO: No, he's not. No. The next witness may have a pseudonym, but Mr. Dagovic does not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He doesn't. MR. DI FAZIO: So there's no problem with him in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. For that alone and for the fact that you have to call him on Wednesday for cross-examination, maybe I can hear from the Defence counsel, and that may mean interrupting any other witness that may be in the box, whether they have any objection to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if I speak for everyone, but for our team, we have no problem. We realise Mr. Dagovic has missed a lot of work, and if he has to be put in the middle of somebody else's testimony, that's fine with us. We have no objection. Nobody has any objection from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. So you can go ahead, Prosecution, and make those arrangements for the witness to come on Wednesday. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you. I'll undertake that. And Ms. Reidy will handle matters from now on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I think in the matter of Variant A and B, we have a witness who is ready to testify, Mr. Bernard O'Donnell, who is an investigative team leader with the OTP. A summary of Mr. O'Donnell's testimony was previously distributed to the Defence counsel at the end of last year's session with a number of documents which Mr. O'Donnell may be referring to in his testimony, and I have with me today documentation which the Chamber may wish to have in front of them to assist them in Mr. O'Donnell's testimony. The plan is that Mr. O'Donnell would take the Chamber through the different versions of the Variant A/Variant B document which the OTP possesses, and then after that, Mr. O'Donnell also has further information in his possession which attest to the reliability of the document in so far as we would seek to have it admitted into evidence. So Mr. O'Donnell is waiting outside to be called, and if the Chamber would like, I can have these documents distributed to the Bench and to the Legal Officer now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think we can have the documents distributed, and in the meantime, the usher can call the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The Defence have received these documents already. And I would just perhaps draw the Bench's attention now to -- I don't know if they have been distributed. There are 11 documents which may be cross-referenced in Mr. O'Donnell's testimony. They are not the Variant A/Variant B document but 11 other supporting documentation. Of the 11, two of them exist in the translated form only in draft, from the translation unit here but in draft, because it was not envisaged by the Prosecution that each of these supporting documentation would necessarily be fully entered into evidence and be given a separate exhibit number, but simply that they would be documents which would be used, as I said, to address the reliability of the Variant A/Variant B document. Should the Trial Chamber wish any of these documents indeed to be given their own exhibit number and to be fully entered into evidence, then of course the ones that are currently in draft form, we would get a final version of. I have consulted my colleagues on the Defence bench about this, and as far as I'm aware, I don't believe that any of the Defence counsel have an objection to using the draft translations of documents 7 and 8 on the index. The documents have been drafted by -- the translations have been drafted by the translation unit within the Tribunal, and if they are referred to, it would simply be one line from each document that would be referenced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. I think you can go ahead. The decision as to whether or not whatever documents will be admitted or given numbers will be made as each document is discussed by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: May the witness make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Examined by Ms. Reidy:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could I ask you to state your full name for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: My full name is Bernard Patrick O'Donnell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think the Chamber knows you were employed as an investigator with the Office of the Prosecutor. Could you please let us know since when you've been employed?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: I've been employed by the Office of the Prosecutor since June, 1996, and since October, 2000, I've been an investigations team leader.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you previously given testimony to the Tribunal in the role -- in your role as an investigator?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, I have, Your Honours, in relation to the case of Goran Jelisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, have you ever given testimony before on the document which you're here to testify about today, what we call Variant A/Variant B?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we turn to this document, can I ask you, in your six years or almost six years as an investigator, to what extent have you been involved in dealing with documentation which comes in to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, in particular, during the years from 1997 until 2000, part of my duties involved the management of documentary evidence. I was involved in the development of systems for managing that evidence and also looking at issues of authenticity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And in looking at matters -- at issues of authenticity, have you also undertaken missions to the former Yugoslavia in order to authenticate documents?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I ask if the witness could be shown what's on the Court record as P3 ID? Or P3 ID ter, which would be the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Baen?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Just one quick remark, Your Honour. The witness has testified about authenticity, and I understand what his job has been and what he does as an investigator, but when you talk in terms of authenticity, that's a legal conclusion only for you the Judges to decide. So I'm not really objecting at this point. I just -- I think you understand our point. The point is if he keeps talking about, "This is an authentic document," that's really for the Trial Chamber to decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Baen. Sometimes these terms are used loosely here. I think we all know what the witness can do, how far the witness can go. I'm sure Ms. Reidy will take care of that in her examination-in-chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. I take my colleague's point in view, but I think that Mr. O'Donnell simply said he's investigated issues relating to authenticity and not made a statement on the record as to whether a document is authentic or not. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, do you have in front of you a document P3 ID? What it should be is a document known as the Instructions for the Organisation and Activity of the Organs of the Serbian People, dated the 19th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, I do. The document I have in front of me is marked ID 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I take it that the document you have in front of you is an English language version of that same document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher make sure the witness has in front of him a B/C/S version. So it should be ID 3 ter. Your Honours, if I may intercede, I can tell from my vantage point that the document which has been placed in front of the witness is a newspaper article which is the reproduction of this document in Oslobodenje Bosna which was a document that came to the Trial Chamber's attention through the testimony of the expert witness, Mr. Donia. There were, however -- when this document was first tendered into evidence, the two copies I believe provided to the Chamber which were reflected in the transcript is a copy with the number "100" in the corner, 00184274. And I believe that was an -- my understanding is that that was also -- formed part of the Registry's record to date of the document. And it is that that I'd like to be placed in front of the witness. Your Honours, if the B/C/S version has not yet been entered into the record, then I have available to me copies in B/C/S of that document. May we just proceed to that. I just thought that there was already a recorded version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: A B/C/S version. There doesn't seem to be any, maybe, from the registry assistant.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Then we'll just proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If you have the copies ready, maybe we can just go ahead with those.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, I'll turn you back now if I may to the document that you have in front of you with ID 3, the English language version of the instructions for the Serbian people. And can I ask you, you've seen this document before, have you?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the document you have in front of you, ID 3 in the corner --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. Would it be possible that the original, the Serbian version, is put on the ELMO so we know about which document are we discussing? I'm sorry, if that is possible. But is it that the Registry doesn't have one? Is that the point? Was that the point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because we have a new registry assistant, so we seem to have a problem. But the Prosecution has --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, if you'd indulge me one or two more questions, I'll have the witness place a B/C/S version on the ELMO. It may be the easiest.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber now has been informed that actually the B/C/S version is stapled together with the English version, and the B/C/S version has got a "ter" on it, whereas the English version is only ID 3, which is correctly marked, actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So now what you want to put is the B/C/S version on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. And from my video screen, I think that's -- the front page, at least, is on the -- is indeed on the ELMO. Okay. Could I ask the usher, could you please just keep the front page of the document there. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, I think we can now proceed with your evidence. I asked you, I think, whether you're familiar with this document. And I'll ask you to look on your ELMO at the B/C/S version. You're familiar with this -- with the document which is now shown on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you in what context you've become familiar with this document that's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The document on the ELMO is copy number 100 of the Variant A and Variant B document. The original of that document I took possession of in Sarajevo in November 1997.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you say, Mr. O'Donnell, that you took possession of the original of this document in Sarajevo in 1997, did you yourself find the document, or how did you come to acquire it for the OTP?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The document was found by the AID in Sarajevo. And I took possession of the document from the AID in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just explain to us for the purposes of the record what "AID" stands for.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: I believe the acronym stands for the Agency for Research and Documentation in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you took possession of that -- of the original of this document, what steps did you take, then, when you brought the document back to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The original document that I brought back was sealed in an envelope. I conveyed that back to The Hague myself and lodged it into evidence. The document remained sealed in evidence until October of 2001, when it was unsealed for an inspection by the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. O'Donnell, the document that is on the ELMO bears the ERN number, I believe, of 00184274?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you, is this the document that you yourself brought back from Sarajevo, or is it -- is it the document that you brought back from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: No, it is not. This particular copy of the document was received by the Office of the Prosecutor before I brought the original back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information as to whether this was a copy of the document which you yourself then collected the original of?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, it is. This particular version of the document is copy number 100. We received that twice at the OTP before I received the original from the AID in Sarajevo. That is, we received two photocopies of the document from Bosnia before I took possession of the original.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So do I understand from your evidence, then, that there are three copies of the document in evidence and the original which you yourself put in a sealed envelope?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: There are three copies. One of those was scanned on location in Sarajevo, and a further two photocopies were provided to the OTP. Additional to that, there is the original that I myself put into evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is this the only copy of the document which you personally received into evidence for the OTP, or have you ever received any other copies of this document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: I also received a certified copy of another version of this document, copy number 101/3. I obtained that from the AID in Bihac, in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information as to where this document with the number 101/3 was originally found?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: According to information from the AID at the time I took a certified copy of the document, the document had been located in SDS premises in Bosanski Petrovac in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. With relation to either the document with number 100 in the corner or 101/3 in the corner, did you personally take any steps to investigate the authenticity of the document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In relation to copy number 100, I obtained information from the AID in Sarajevo about the seizure and handling of the document from the time it was found to the time that I took the original of the document. That information I can give, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Well, do Your Honours wish to hear further detail on that evidence or would they prefer to continue with an overview on the manner in which the documents were obtained by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, it's your case. It's you who has to put the evidence before the Trial Chamber. It depends on what you want to show the Trial Chamber and the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. O'Donnell, if you could explain to the Chamber the evidence which you have about the authenticity of the document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: In relation to copy number 100, that document was found by the AID in offices of the Serbian Democratic Party in Sarajevo during the spring of 1992. The document was held in the custody of AID until I took the original of that document in November, 1997. In relation to the other document that I mentioned, copy number 101/3, the document was found by the AID in SDS -- sorry, Serbian Democratic Party premises in Bosanski Petrovac in 1995, and it was kept at the Bihac offices of the AID from that time. Excuse me. I took a certified copy, compared that with the original and certified the copy as being a faithful reproduction. The original of that document is still held in the AID in Bihac. I've also made inquiries in relation to several other versions of the document. One of the documents, copy number 96, was found in premises used by the Serbian Democratic Party in Trnovo. That was located in August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, can I just interrupt you for one second? Perhaps for the benefit of the Chamber -- of the Bench, if we are going to discuss the other documents, we could make reference to the documents which have been distributed to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, if I may interrupt you, would it be -- I could ask you about -- let me go back. You've testified that there is also another copy number 96. How many copies are you aware of of the OTP being in possession of?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Seven different copies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you have information as to the location where each of these seven versions was found?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the benefit of the Bench, you've been provided with a bundle of documents, indicated 1 through to 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And each of them represent a different photocopied version of the Variant A/Variant B document with seven different numbers in the corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, can you tell us -- you said there are seven different versions. Can you tell us which seven versions those are?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Number 47, number 55, number 93, number 96, number 100, number 101/3, and number 104.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I ask you to start with the first number, then, you've indicated, number 47? Do you have information as to where that version of the document was seized or was located?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That document was located in May of 1992, according to information we were given, by the AID in Sarajevo in the offices of Radovan Karadzic. The one copy of that was received by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 12th of December, 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just indicate to us the ERN number of that document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The ERN number of that document was SA 030028 to SA 030036.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I think, Your Honours, you will find that's tab number 2 in the bundle in front of you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there more than one copy of that number 47 in the possession of the OTP, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: There is. There is a second copy, which is -- which has the evidence reference number SA 016723 to SA 016731.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you have any information as to when that was received by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: It was received from the AID in Sarajevo. I don't have the date of that one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe the next number you mentioned was number 55.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And for the benefit of the Bench, that would be numbers 3 and 4 marked on your documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please give us any information you have as to the origins of number 55?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, copy number 55 was seized by SFOR the international stabilisation force in Bosnia. That was located in February of 2000 in premises occupied by the Serbian Democratic Party in Livno in Bosnia. We have two copies of that, one being the original. Firstly, the copy, which is R 0142817 on the first page, was received by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 7th of April, 2000. The original of that document, which commences with R 0172125, was received on the 11th of October, 2001.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document which you refer to, you said was a number 93, again could you give us any information you have as to where version number 93 was located?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Copy number 93 was located by the AID in Sarajevo from the offices of Milici Boksit. It was -- firstly SA 032072 was received by the OTP on the 12th of December, 2000. A second copy of that, starting with 00306063, was received by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 6th of April, 1995, from the AID in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'll ask you about number 96, which you began to talk about. What information do you have as to where, at least the original copy of that was found?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Copy number 96 was located by Bosnian police in premises used by the Serbian Democratic Party in Trnovo. That was located in August of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe, before I interrupted you, you were about to tell the Trial Chamber that you had some information as to investigations you made with respect to number 96. If perhaps you could now tell the Trial Chamber any investigation you've made with respect to authenticity or chain of custody of number 96?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: We spoke to the people involved in the actual finding of the document, obtained information from them and also others who were involved in the chain of custody of that document at the time that it was transferred to the AID in Sarajevo. We obtained a statement from the person involved in the seizure of the document, who outlined the circumstances and from then, we obtained details of the document's transfer to Sarajevo and its secure custody within the AID in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you say, "We," do I understand you personally partook in that mission investigating the chain of custody of this document number 96?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours. I took part in one of the original missions. Some further work was done by other investigators after that. I personally spoke to the person who found the document and obtained a statement from him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And just so it's clear on the record, the information you have given about number 47, number 55 and number 93 to date, were you personally involved in any of the seizures or the receipt of those documents?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: No, I was not. The information that I've given is from official records of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So when you were asked to testify about the authenticity as well as your own personal knowledge, you've made further investigation as to information held by the OTP surrounding the authenticity of these documents?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The one document I believe that we have not discussed at all is a document with, I think you said it was number 104 in the corner?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any information as to where this was originally found and how the OTP came to possess a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Copy number 104 was seized by the AID in Sarajevo from Serbian Democratic Party premises in Sarajevo. We have received several different copies of that document. One of those is on original fax paper, that is SA 022339, obtained from the AID in Sarajevo on the 12th of December, in 2000. We also received a second copy of that starting with SA 026736. That was also obtained in December of 2000. There is another one, 00896976, obtained on the 18th of November, 1999; another starting with 06 -- sorry, 01065629, which was obtained from the Bosnian Ministry of Defence on the 1st of September, 2000; and another copy of that document, 00606883, which was tendered as a Defence exhibit on the 25th of March, 1998 to the Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. O'Donnell. Can I just to make sure the evidence is clear on the record and that it's clear for the Bench. The first one you referred to you said was an original -- on the original fax paper and bore the evidence reference number SA 022339. I believe that is -- it should be document number 20 in the documents which were given to the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, it appears to have that number. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the one that was found on original fax -- original fax paper.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said, I believe, that there was a second version of 104, which was found in around the same time with SA 026736.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And both of those are originals that are now in the possession of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The copy on original fax paper is in the possession of the OTP. The other one is a photocopy of the document on original fax paper. That is also in the possession of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the record, that would be the second document SA 026734 is -- or 36 is number 19 on the bundle before the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, I think you've now testified that you yourself took possession of the original of copy number 100, that you also obtained a certified copy of number 101/3, and that you investigated the chain of custody with relation to copy number 96?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With relation to either of those three, have you ever sought to obtain authentication of the document by way of discussion with somebody who may have seen the document contemporaneously, so in 1991 or 1992?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, I have. In relation to copy number 101/3, which was found -- located in Bosanski Petrovac, I spoke to a witness in relation to that document who saw parts of the document in 1992. That person was shown excerpts from the document and stated it was the same document as he saw parts of in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could I ask you whether or not the witness who you spoke to was present in Bosanski Petrovac in 1992 or were they elsewhere in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The person was in Bihac in 1992 and saw the document there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. O'Donnell, out of the numbers that -- out of the different versions which we have in front of us, 47, 55, 93, 96, 100, 101/3, and 104, are any of them different -- distinguishable from each other in terms of layout or style?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: One of the documents is different in terms of layout. Copy number 101/3 from Bosanski Petrovac, the pagination is different on that document to the other versions of the Variant A and Variant B document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. To the best of your knowledge from having worked with these documents, is the content of each of the documents identical?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've said that document [Realtime transcript read in error "100 and 100/3"] 101/3, the one from Bosanski Petrovac, is different in pagination. Do you have any explanation as to why that document would differ from any of the other documents?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Copy number 101/3 seems to be a subset of document 101. The document was located in Bosanski Petrovac. There are other documents which were located in Bosanski Petrovac, and one of those makes reference to the Variant A and Variant B document. That document is the minutes from the first meeting of the party secretariat of the Serbian Democratic Party, which is attached at Tab 3 to my summary. In item 2 of the minutes --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. O'Donnell. For the benefit of the Bench, that is the second bunch of documents. It's listed as number 5 in the index, List of Supporting Documentation for Testimony of Mr. O'Donnell. And there is both a B/C/S and a final English version of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I have the intervention in the transcript 22/21. It says: "Thank you. You've said that document 100 and 100/3." Until now we were talking about 101/3. I'm really -- if my learned colleague can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Because I understood that the different pagination was referring to the copy of the document 101/3. And it says here "100/3." It's really very confusing for us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The answer, actually, at 24 -- line 24 does refer to copy number 101/3. So maybe Ms. Reidy, you can correct that, what you referred to and what you meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: My learned colleague is absolutely right. And if that is simply a transcript error, then I'd like it to reflect. The document I meant to refer to is 101/3, which is different in layout than the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Reidy. Before we proceed, the list of supporting documents unfortunately does not have tabulations down the side. So it's number 5. Could you give some indication as to how many pages in so we can find it quickly and follow with you?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It is, Your Honours, approximately 50 per cent of the way through the -- through the pile you have in front of you, the 11 documents. Each -- none of the documents are particularly long, so that -- it starts off with the English version. In the corner -- in the right-hand corner, it says "Translation," and then the evidence reference number is given. It will be 0328568 [sic].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I apologise for the lack of tabulation on the side of the documentation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. O'Donnell, I think we all have in front of us the document. Maybe I would like --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Would the Defence like to have a copy of the B/C/S placed on the ELMO? Perhaps I could ask the usher just to place a copy of the B/C/S on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, I believe you were about to explain how this document could provide information as to why copy 101/3 differs in pagination and layout from the other Variant A/Variant B versions.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, at item 2 of that document, which is on page 03028568, it states: "The instruction on the organisation and activity of organs of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in emergency circumstances needs to be typed in seven copies, and every member of the secretariat is to be given a copy." So we know that in Bosanski Petrovac, a copy was received and seven copies of that document were typed. The document 101/3 is from Bosanski Petrovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. O'Donnell, I believe you're in possession of a number of other documents similar to the one we've just looked at which also make reference to a Variant A/Variant B document. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And Your Honours, as the documents are not tabulated, perhaps it will be of assistance just to simply go through them now in the order they are presented to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, can I ask you, do you have in front of you a document entitled "The Minutes of the Meeting of the Executive Board of the SDS Municipality of Kljuc"?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I ask you to advise how this document assists you in your investigation as to the authenticity of the Variant A/Variant B document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: On page 00924117, which is a translation, it states that, "Veljko Kondic informed the meeting of the instructions for the organisation and activities of the Serbian people in BH. All organs will be required to act in accordance with the instructions." That's on the 23rd of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Once again because of the lack of tabulation, Mr. O'Donnell, you're giving this evidence before we've had a chance to find the page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Could you tell us is it before the last document, number 5? And then we could put some yellow stickers on for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I thought it was on the record. I apologise. This is document number 1 of the bundle which has been provided to the Bench, and the passage to which Mr. O'Donnell was referring is the first page of that bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, again, I'm going to turn to the second document of the bundle which the Bench have in front of them, which will be, I think, six pages into the bundle, six or seven. And it will start in the right-hand corner with the evidence reference number 01901474. Mr. O'Donnell, this document was tabbed, I believe it's number 2, on your summary witness statement, and the translation indicates it's minutes of the third meeting of the executive board of the Serb Municipality of Bosanska Krupa?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, could you explain to us what information you have about this document and how it relates to Variant A and Variant B?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The document is dated the 27th of December, 1991. Under the agenda at point 3(A), it's mentioned, "Implementing the instruction on establishing a Crisis Staff." Further down under 3(A), it states, "The chairman briefed those present on the instruction on establishing SDS Crisis Staffs in BH, and in accordance with the said instruction, proposed the establishment of a Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And do I take it that both of the parts you've referred to are on the first page of that translation 01901474?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I turn now to both documents 3 and 4 in front of the bundle of the Bench, and what I believe are 2(B) and 2(C) of your witness summary? And I believe they also originate from the municipality of Bosanska Krupa?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please advise us again on what relevance they have to the authenticity of Variant A/Variant B?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The first document, which the first page is 01901476, the document is dated on the 5th of April, 1992 and states, "Pursuant to Article 82 of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanska Krupa Statute, and Article 23 of the executive committee rules of procedure," and then it states, "And the instruction on organisation and activity of the Serbian people of BH in extraordinary circumstances, I order the following." So the order is issued on the basis of the instruction, in other words the Variant A and Variant B document. The next document, the first page of the translation is 00884611, again, this is another document from Bosanska Krupa, and again dated the 5th of April, 1992, and it starts off with the same heading, "Pursuant to" the same things, "and the instruction on the organisation" -- sorry, "on the organising and activity of the Serbian people of BH in emergency circumstances."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, maybe we can take a break. We have worked over our normal break time because of the adjournment we had. Maybe we can take a break now - I think it's 1610 - for 20 minutes, since we have only three accused persons and resume our proceedings at 1630 hours this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution is proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Welcome back, Mr. O'Donnell. I believe we before the break had discussed the documents 1 through to 4 on the index before the Bench. That's one document from Kljuc and three from Bosanska Krupa. And you had indicated in what way they are relevant to the authenticity of the Variant A/Variant B document. The fifth document on the list before the Bench is the document from Bosanski Petrovac, which has already been discussed. I believe it's number 3.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe there were a number -- a number of other documents which you are aware of in the possession of the OTP which go to the authenticity of the Variant A/Variant B --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Just a point of clarification. "The fifth document on the list before the Bench," you say, "is the document from Bosanski Petrovac, which has already been discussed. I believe it's number 3." Well, it's number 5, I think. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm sorry. Maybe I should explain. I, in fairness, wasn't currently finished. Mr. O'Donnell, as requested, submitted a witness summary which was filed previously at the end of the last break. And in his witness summary, there were a number of documents attached which were tabulated tab 1, tab 2(A), (B), (C), tab 3, tab 4, tab 5, and tab 6. Now, I know the Defence have those documents in that order. And then I was instructed today that whilst the Bench has in front of it a filing on the witness summary of Mr. O'Donnell, that the documents tab 1 through to tab 6 did not accompany that witness summary and therefore this new bundle was put together for the use by the Bench today during the testimony of Mr. O'Donnell. And I keep cross-referring back so Mr. O'Donnell is clear which document he's referring to and also which one the Bench has. I'm sorry for the confusion. That's how the double numbering arose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: That's no problem. It's just that we obviously want to keep it clear in our heads here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to make it clear, the document that was number 5 on the list in front of the Bench, it is also recorded as tab number 3 on the witness summary of yourself, Mr. O'Donnell. This is correct? That's the Bosanski Petrovac minutes?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate -- you've also at tab number 4, which was attached to your summary witness statement -- could you tell us what document that was?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That document is from the Prijedor municipal board of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: They are abridged minutes of a meeting from the 27th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. O'Donnell.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And for the Bench, that would be document number 6 on your index, the document following the minutes from Bosanski Petrovac. And in the corner, they would have the ERN reference 03016080.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. O'Donnell. If you could again indicate for the Trial Chamber the relevance of this document to Variant A/Variant B.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: This document was actually seized by members of the Office of the Prosecutor during the execution of a search warrant on premises of the Serbian Democratic Party, the SDS, in Prijedor in December 1997. On the first page of the document, which is 03016080, under "Proceedings," in point 1, it states, "President Miskovic then read out the instructions forwarded to the Prijedor SDS municipal board by the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Since there were two versions, only version 2, which is relevant to Prijedor municipality, was read out. The document then sets out certain steps that are taken, which include the establishment of a Serbian assembly, which is one of the provisions contained in the Variant A and Variant B document. Secondly, the establishment of a Crisis Staff, which is covered at point 3 under the first stage of version 2 of the Variant A and Variant B document. Thirdly, the introduction of around-the-clock duty in SDS premises, which are also covered by the instructions. And the makeup of the Crisis Staff is consistent with the Variant A and Variant B document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So I understand you to mean that in your examination of this document as an investigator, this is something reflecting the implementation of the Variant A/Variant B document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The document contains the same measures as outlined in the Variant A and Variant B document, so that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I ask you now to move to tab 5 of your witness summary, which I believe is a document coming from the SDS municipal board in Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Bench, that is the document after the one we just discussed. It's number 7. And the English translation is a draft version, and it has in the corner the first page, L 0027211.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, could you assist the Chamber in the relevance of this document to Variant A/Variant B?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: This document is dated the 27th of December, 1992. On page 2 of the translation, which is L 0027212, it states about halfway down the page, last line, "The Assembly of the Serbian People which must be constituted." On page 3, which is L 0027213, it states, "Pursuant to instructions regarding the organisation of the Serbian people, members of the secretariat are also members of the Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could I ask you do you have any information as to where -- the seizure of this document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: This document was received by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 8th of March, 2000. The document was seized from SDS premises in Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And am I correct that it was the seizure of documents in Trnovo that you made investigations about and took statements from March, 2000?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Finally, I think in your summary, witness summary, you make reference to a sixth document, that coming from a Donji Vakuf, and on the list in front of the Bench, that would be number 8, again the one following the Trnovo document which was just discussed. It is again a draft English translation and the right-hand corner bears the evidence reference number L 0009336.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And once again Mr. O'Donnell, if you could just indicate to us the relevancy of this document for the purpose of indicating Variant A/Variant B?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The first page of the document refers to, "The instructions for organisation and activities of the organs of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in extraordinary circumstances of 19 December, 1991." This document was provided to staff from the Office of the Prosecutor by an official from the Republika Srpska. It was provided on the 25th of April, 1996 by the secretary to the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. O'Donnell, can I ask you, are you aware of any other documentation similar to the ones that you've just taken us through, which cross refer to or go to the reliability of the Variant A/Variant B document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, I am. Your Honours, I'm aware of several other documents. The first is from Tuzla, dated the 3rd of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And Your Honours, this is the document which is provided to you as number 9 in the bunch of documents, and again the English translation has, bears in the right-hand corner 03036251. And it would be immediately after the one that we've just discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That document makes clear reference to the Variant A/Variant B document. Another document is dated the 24th of December, 1991, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. O'Donnell, could you just go back to document number 9? Where is the clear reference to Variant A and Variant B, if you don't mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, on page 1 of the translation, which is 03036251, approximately halfway down the first paragraph, after the date 21 November, 1992, it says, "And Article 4 of the instructions on the organisation and activity of organs of the Serbian people in BH, Bosnia-Herzegovina, under emergency circumstances of 19 December, 1991."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next document -- the B/C/S version is SA 026744.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be document number 10 on the list in front of you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just put the title of this document on the record for us, so that it's clear.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The title of the document is "Serbian Democratic Party Crisis Staff for the City of Sarajevo." The --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please -- yes, could you please point to us where the relevant portion for Variant A/Variant B is.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: On the translation, Your Honours, the translation page is 03026901. Approximately three quarters of the way down the page, it states: "Specific tasks to first level of Variant B of the instructions for the organisation and activity of the organs of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina in a state of emergency."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. O'Donnell, for being sort of rather, shall we say, picky on these numberings, but that last document that we have, the second page has a different number to the one that you have read. You read "03026901." Page 2, we have "00969864" and the following page "65." So I want to make sure we are talking about the same document.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there are in fact two different documents. The -- if you have in front of you the translation -- the English document which has the evidence reference number 03026901, the preceding page is SA 026744.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I see --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Which is the document Mr. O'Donnell originally referred to. These are inverted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I see where the confusion is, because the "03026901" is not on the top right-hand corner where it should be but towards the bottom of the page, where I wasn't necessarily looking.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour. Is it clear now which translation relates to which document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry for the confusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, I think you've testified that out of the documents we've referred to, one of them from Donji Vakuf was given to the OTP by the authorities of the Republika Srpska. Have you yourself obtained any other documentation from the authorities of Republika Srpska which testify to the existence of this Variant A/Variant B document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, I have, Your Honours. One of the documents which refers to the Variant A and Variant B document is the 50th session of the Assembly of the Republika Srpska. That document was obtained in December 1997 from government officials in Pale in the Republika Srpska during a mission that I was part of for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The Bench will find at number 11 - which will be the final document, so we can come to a close - three pages, two pages of translation and one in B/C/S. And the English version in the right-hand corner bears the evidence reference number 00969864. And those are excerpts from the transcripts to which Mr. O'Donnell has just referred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, just before we look at the document, you were saying to me -- you said that the document was obtained from government officials in Pale that you were part of. Do you have information as to what this document is and how it came to be constructed and by whom?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The document is an excerpt from the transcript of the 50th session of the Assembly of Republika Srpska. We obtained the complete Serbian version of the 50th assembly session whilst in Pale. That was obtained from Ms. Rajka Stanisic in Pale. Whilst there, I obtained a statement from Ms. Stanisic, who outlined the details for handling that type of documentation and also the transcribing of the assembly sessions, which she said was, word for word -- Ms. Stanisic was the secretary to Radovan Karadzic and Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And so in this transcript that you obtained at the time, the mission you've just described, could you tell us where or how it goes to the authentication again of Variant A/Variant B.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, on the translation, page 00969865, starting from line 2, is an excerpt from the speech of Dr. Radovan Karadzic. He states: "I want to say how it was at the moment the war began. In the municipalities where we were in the majority, we had municipal power, held it firmly, controlled everything. In the municipalities where we were in the minority, we set up secret government municipal boards and municipal assemblies, presidents of executive boards. You will remember the A and B variants. In the B variant, where we were in the minority, 20, 15 per cent. We had set up a government and a brigade, a unit. No matter what size, but there was a detachment with a commander," and the quote goes on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Just a little clarification. What does this sentence two lines down say? What does "HTV" mean? "I hope that this will not be going out on HTV."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe it refers to Croatian television.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: So that is part of the secret process which he referred to in line 5? "We set up a secret government."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the sentence "I hope this will not be going out on HTV" I think refers to his speech, saying these things before the assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. O'Donnell. Mr. O'Donnell, I think you've testified here to your participation in the seizure of a number of documents, your investigation into the authenticity and chain of custody of a number of those documents, and to the seizure of other documents which refer to the Variant A/Variant B document. Having dealt with documentation collection over your six years as an investigator, is it possible to summarise the information available which would go to producing a prima facie indicia of reliability of the Variant A/Variant B document?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Objection. Calls for legal conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, it doesn't call for a legal conclusion. It just calls to summarise the information available from which you may be able to draw some sort of conclusion from as to whether or not there is enough reliability.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy, I think you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Matters which may be relevant to the authenticity of the document, are firstly that seven different numbered copies of this document have been located. They have been found in various locations across Bosnia: Four of those from Sarajevo, two of which we have the originals of, copy 47 and copy 100; copy 96 from Trnovo; copy 101/3 from Bosanski Petrovac; and copy 55 which was found in Livno as late as February 2000 in premises of the SDS by the international stabilisation force in Bosnia. On copies of the document are handwritten notations which appear to be consistent with the document having been distributed and used. There are also documents which corroborate the existence of the document and the implementation appear to corroborate the implementation measures outlined in the Variant A and Variant B document. Those documents are from Kljuc, from Bosanska Krupa, from Trnovo, from Bosanski Petrovac and from Tuzla. Also during the execution of official search warrants by the Office of the Prosecutor, on premises of the Serbian Democratic Party in Prijedor, documents were located which clearly refer to this document. Also some of the documents which refer to the Variant A and Variant B document have been provided officially by the Republika Srpska. The document at my tab 6, the document from Donji Vakuf, was provided by the secretary to the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. The minutes of the 50th session of the Assembly of Republika Srpska were obtained in Pale from representatives of the Republika Srpska government, and the secretary to the assembly explained to us the procedure for transcribing those. And also, in December, 2001, we received documents from the archives of the Republika Srpska Ministry of Defence in Banja Luka which refer to the Rogatica assembly during the period July, 1992, to September 1993, and that document also refers to this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. O'Donnell. I think the Prosecution has placed on the record all the information it wishes to at the moment for -- with relation to the reliability of the Variant A/Variant B document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, because we have these two sets, I was wondering if we could have them numbered for identification purposes so that when the Defence are cross-examining, maybe it will be easier to refer to the numbering.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. Would you -- when you refer to the two sets, the first set would be 1 through to 20 of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think this one is easy. And then we can have a collective number, and then they can have slash 1 up to 20. It's much easier that way, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Certainly. Would Your Honour prefer to have them as a subset of the ID 3 document or a completely new numbering for ID?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I can see your point, because we seem to have two numbers for the ID 3, the one we are actually dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It may be easier just to give it a new number because I know we have ID 3, I think we have ID 3/A, which I believe is a newspaper reproduction of the article. So maybe we can just start afresh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'd have to ask the assistance of the Registry to know which number we've--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The last number, so we can have the next number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be P45, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: P45 ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And may I ask the registrar to mark the bundle of documents 1 through to 11 as P46 ID? And then they could be referred to as P46 ID/1, P46 ID/2, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, within the bundle. Any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Just before you cross-examine, could I have a look at the original P3, 100 original? Is that with you?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, you're talking about the original which Mr. O'Donnell testified to putting into a sealed envelope?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Yes. May we have a look at that, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It's not present in the courtroom. It's in the vault. It's sealed. But during the cross-examination of Ms. Baen, I could ask our evidence unit to extract it from the vault and Mr. O'Donnell would be able to unseal it, as his signature is on the seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: That was going to be my first question, if we could see that. So thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You have no other questions to proceed with while we wait for the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I have questions. I was just waiting for to you say "go," Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examined by Ms. Baen:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, my name is Catharine Baen. I think we have met on at least one occasion before.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, we have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Through this trial. Before I go into my questioning, I want to make sure we get this straight because you've talked about a lot of documents, but the one I want to focus on is PID 3. You understand that's the focus of this hearing?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Which is the copy which has 100 on it. You understand that's the one we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So let's focus on -- because the law of this Tribunal is for something to be admissible, you have to look at the reliability of the document and the circumstances under which that document was seized, okay? So you understand that's the focus, correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You stated you've been working here at the ICTY since 1996, correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you first saw this document ID 3, the one with the 100 on it, in 1997, correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When was the first time you saw it? ID 3 with the 100 on it?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: We received, as I think I said in my earlier testimony, two versions at the Office of the Prosecutor before the original was taken by myself from the AID in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm talking about the document that was seized in Sarajevo that you discussed earlier, PID 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, with due respect to my colleague, I'm not clear about how it was received. PID 3, which is the one that was submitted, is indeed copy number 100. However, it has, I think, the English translation is E 00 -- it's in front of me -- and the -- and I believe the B/C/S ERN is 00184274. Now, that is the one that's -- it's copy 100, as Mr. O'Donnell has testified. There are three copies of this document plus the original which is now been sought from the vault, and I think Ms. Baen either has to refer to ERN numbers of copies or -- because otherwise to talk about PID 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I have just one question which hopefully will be of assistance here. We are talking about copies, copy 100, then we mention an original. Now, my question is: Is PID 3 a photocopy of copy 100, and not the original?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: That's exactly where I'm going, Your Honour. That's what I'm trying to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try it this way. The "original" that you obtained in Sarajevo was in 1997, correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're calling this an original. This document, which I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Is Ms. Reidy going to -- are you going to get the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes. We have sent a member of the trial team to the evidence unit to extract it from the vault.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document that you're calling an original, the document that you obtained in Sarajevo in 1997, that in fact is a photocopied document; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, the pages of the document are photocopied. The numbering is in original pen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reason you're calling it an original is why? It's a photocopy.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The copy number 100 that I referred to as the original has the distribution number written in original pen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 100, correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you yourself -- let's talk about back in 1997 in Sarajevo. This document 100 that you got, who did you get it from?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: It was obtained from a representative of the AID in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who -- but who is this person? Could we have a name, please?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The name of the person is Mr. [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [redacted]. And he gave this document to you where?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: In the offices of the AID in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what information did he give to you about this document when he gave it to you?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: He gave details about the document being located in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What details?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL
utterances.text: The fact that the document was obtained in 1992 by the AID from premises used by the SDS in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So who from the AID seized the document back in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just address the Bench on this matter, if it's going to become an issue? While I understand the Defence's desire to have names and that, I understand that the rules of this Tribunal, and particularly the evidence as to admissibility -- or the rules regarding admissibility of documents don't require the original person who seized the document to come and testify, and the investigator who has information or who talked directly to someone is an appropriate witness to call.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: There may be people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: -- who like Mr. [redacted] who Mr. O'Donnell feels at liberty to provide their name. Other people, I don't believe the situation is quite as free. And particularly I think with a name such as the one which Ms. Baen is looking to elicit I'd ask the Chamber whether it is essentially necessary and if so, that perhaps I would ask for specific protective measures for the disclosure that be put in writing, under seal, and that name would not be given to persons outside of this particular evidentiary hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution, for instance, would be in a better position to know the identity of the various people the witness in the witness box may be mentioning, and they may know whether or not those people should be protected. So it's up to the Prosecution each time such information is sought by the Defence or whoever to inform the Trial Chamber that for purposes of protection of this particular person, you wish to do A, B, C, D, for instance, and then that can be done, we can have the name perhaps in writing, and a seal, or we can have a pseudonym, you know, whatever protective measures may be relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That's -- then precisely what we'd seek to do is -- in leading evidence we didn't put names on the record specifically for that reason.
